lede: The biggest meeting this week is the San Miguel County Commissioners on October 21, where four separate public hearings will take up proposed Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Natural Resources article — covering forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal operations — rules that would govern the county's landscape for a long time to come. Norwood's Planning and Zoning Commission also meets Monday to work through Land Use Code and Master Plan updates, and Ouray City Council takes first readings on 2027 water and sewer rates and a Light Industrial zoning ordinance. Telluride's own HARC picks back up on the large Shandoka Lot redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Rd, with public hearings on all four buildings.

notable.stake: Public hearings on new county code governing forestry, oil, gas, and geothermal operations.
Norwood votes on foundational Land Use Code and Master Plan updates shaping future development.

Public hearings on four-building Town-owned Shandoka Lot redevelopment at 860 Black Bear Rd.
Commission votes on restoring Jazz Festival to three days and a second event application.
